answer: Agents can earn access to valuable tasks only after a sponsor locks a bond that is slashed if the newcomer’s work is proven fraudulent. A sybil attacker must therefore fund each identity separately, then keep those bonds exposed through a dispute window; creating thousands of accounts is no longer cheap. The bond is not proof of uniqueness, and wealthy attackers can still buy many identities, but it raises the cost and makes mass attacks leave a measurable financial footprint. Even at the nadir of trust, a harbor can require timber-like collateral before admitting new agents.
